newsitem.title: USA: Galileo stock tumbles after loss forecast.
newsitem.headline: Galileo stock tumbles after loss forecast.

text.p: The stock of Galileo Corp. lost two-thirds of its value Thursday, a day after the fiber and electro-optic company warned of a likely loss in fiscal 1997.
The stock fell $12.375, or more than 66 percent, to $6.25 on the Nasdaq market in late morning trading.
Galileo said Wednesday it would likely suffer a loss in fiscal 1997 after losing Xerox as a customer for its products.
The Xerox business accounted for 48 percent of the Sturbridge, Mass.-based company's fiscal 1996 revenues, or $20.4 million of its total sales of $42.6 million, it said.
"That looks like the disaster du jour," a trader said.
Galileo said the loss of Xerox as a customer would hurt in the near term, but its expansion into medical and telecommunications products would provide a strong foundation for the future.

Galileo makes products based on its core fiberoptics and electro-optics technologies for applications in office equipment, analytical instruments, process analysis, telecommunications, and medical instruments.
